title: Perpendicular Lines and the equation of a tangent Flashcards

cards.front: Identify the gradient and y-intercept in the equation $y=mx+c$.

options.explanation: In slope-intercept form, $m$ gives the change in $y$ for each unit increase in $x$, while $c$ is the value of $y$ when $x=0$.
This reverses the roles of the two constants. In $y=mx+c$, $m$ is the gradient because it multiplies $x$, while $c$ is the y-intercept.
The value $-\frac{1}{m}$ would be the gradient of a line perpendicular to this one, not the original line. Its gradient is $m$ and its y-intercept is $c$.
The sign of the intercept must be read directly from the equation. Since the constant term is $+c$, the y-intercept is $c$, while the gradient is $m$.
